claim: A library of 24 yeast strains was constructed that are capable of sending, receiving or responding to three molecular signals.
source: Here, we construct a library of 24 yeast strains capable of sending, receiving or responding to three molecular signals, characterize them experimentally and build quantitative models of their input-output relationships.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the construction of 24 yeast strains with specific capabilities.

claim: Experimentally measured consortia dynamics can be predicted from models of constituent parts.
source: We then compose these strains into two- and three-strain cascades as well as a four-strain bistable switch and show that experimentally measured consortia dynamics can be predicted from the models of the constituent parts.
evidence: The abstract states that experimental measurements match model predictions for multi-strain systems.

claim: Computational search can identify strain combinations that realize target behaviors including logic gates, band-pass filters, and time pulses.
source: To further explore the achievable range of behaviors, we perform a fully automated computational search over all two-, three-, and four-strain consortia to identify combinations that realize target behaviors including logic gates, band-pass filters, and time pulses.
evidence: The abstract describes a computational approach that successfully identifies functional strain combinations.

claim: Experiments closely track computational predictions for optimized strain combinations.
source: Strain combinations that are predicted to map onto a target behavior are further computationally optimized and then experimentally tested. Experiments closely track computational predictions.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states agreement between experimental results and computational predictions.

claim: Single cell circuit engineering has limited scalability because parts cannot be reused.
source: Albeit very successful, single cell circuit engineering has limited scalability and robustness because parts cannot be reused, the genetic burden on the cell grows with circuit size (Nikolados et al., 2019), and retroactivity (Del Vecchio et al., 2008) and component crosstalk (Del Vecchio, 2015) interferes with expected behavior.
evidence: The introduction cites literature to support limitations of single-cell approaches.

claim: Genetic burden on cells grows with circuit size in single-cell circuit engineering.
source: Albeit very successful, single cell circuit engineering has limited scalability and robustness because parts cannot be reused, the genetic burden on the cell grows with circuit size (Nikolados et al., 2019), and retroactivity (Del Vecchio et al., 2008) and component crosstalk (Del Vecchio, 2015) interferes with expected behavior.
evidence: The statement is supported by citation to Nikolados et al., 2019.

claim: Retroactivity interferes with expected behavior in single-cell circuits.
source: Albeit very successful, single cell circuit engineering has limited scalability and robustness because parts cannot be reused, the genetic burden on the cell grows with circuit size (Nikolados et al., 2019), and retroactivity (Del Vecchio et al., 2008) and component crosstalk (Del Vecchio, 2015) interferes with expected behavior.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Del Vecchio et al., 2008.

claim: Component crosstalk interferes with expected behavior in single-cell circuits.
source: Albeit very successful, single cell circuit engineering has limited scalability and robustness because parts cannot be reused, the genetic burden on the cell grows with circuit size (Nikolados et al., 2019), and retroactivity (Del Vecchio et al., 2008) and component crosstalk (Del Vecchio, 2015) interferes with expected behavior.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Del Vecchio, 2015.

claim: Competition over shared gene expression resources makes unrelated circuits unintentionally coupled.
source: Furthermore, competition over shared gene expression resources makes unrelated circuits unintentionally coupled (Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2021.

claim: Division of labor is common in nature.
source: Such division of labor is common in nature and interest has recently emerged in engineering multi-cellular synthetic systems (Brenner et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Three different cell populations can, in theory, generate up to 100 different logic functions.
source: Still, mathematical modeling has demonstrated that multi-cellular computation should easily access a larger space of behaviors: for instance, just three different cell populations can, in theory, generate up to 100 different logic functions (Regot et al., 2011) and even bimodality and cell-synchronization (Thurley et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Regot et al., 2011.

claim: The native BAR1 gene was knocked out to prevent α-factor degradation.
source: To have a baseline strain that does not interfere with signaling, we knocked out the native BAR1 gene as in Youk and Lim, 2014 to prevent α-factor degradation.
evidence: The methods section describes this genetic modification with citation.

claim: FAR1 was knocked out to prevent growth arrest induced by α-factor.
source: Moreover, to account for growth-arrest induced by α-factor, which affects gene expression on a large scale, we knocked out FAR1 a protein that contributes to arresting the cell cycle at G1Chang and Chang and Herskowitz, 1990, and constitutively expressed POG1, a protein that promotes growth-arrest recovery (Leza and Elion, 1999).
evidence: The results section describes this genetic modification with citations.

claim: POG1 was constitutively expressed to promote growth-arrest recovery.
source: Moreover, to account for growth-arrest induced by α-factor, which affects gene expression on a large scale, we knocked out FAR1 a protein that contributes to arresting the cell cycle at G1Chang and Chang and Herskowitz, 1990, and constitutively expressed POG1, a protein that promotes growth-arrest recovery (Leza and Elion, 1999).
evidence: The results section describes this genetic modification with citation to Leza and Elion, 1999.

claim: Overexpression of STE2 solved the problem of no α-factor output from strains that both sense and secrete α-factor.
source: We solved this problem by overexpressing STE2 on a pGPD promoter Sun et al., 2012 in these strains, aiming to have some protein copies escaping this interaction.
evidence: The results section describes this solution with citation.

claim: Integration of the auxin-efflux pump ABCB1/PGP1 from A. thaliana amplified auxin secretion.
source: Here, we amplified Auxin secretion and thus effectively the strength of the signal produced, through integration of the auxin-efflux pump ABCB1/PGP1 from A. thaliana into our yeast strains, as previously reported in Geisler et al., 2005.
evidence: The results section describes this modification with citation.

claim: A significant increase in auxin-synthesis yield was measured when PGP1 was integrated.
source: We measured a significant increase in the auxin-synthesis yield as measured by a neighboring IAA-detecting cell when PGP1 was integrated (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The results section reports experimental data shown in a figure supplement.

claim: GH3.3 from A. thaliana had higher efficiency than GH3.6 in converting IAA to IAA-Asp.
source: We then tested the IAA to IAA-Asp conversion rate using mass spectrometry and found that GH3.3 from A. thaliana had the higher efficiency (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The results section reports experimental data from mass spectrometry shown in a figure supplement.

claim: IAA-Asp does not activate the IAA-mediated degradation pathway in yeast.
source: Finally, we tested that IAA-Asp does not activate the IAA-mediated degradation pathway in yeast, by adding 10 µM of IAA-Asp in an auxin-sensor yeast culture and detecting no variation in fluorescence (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The results section reports experimental data shown in a figure supplement.

claim: The sensors achieve an ON/OFF fold-change that ranges between a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 42.
source: Finally, the sensors achieve an ON/OFF fold-change that ranges between a minimum of 3 (IAA activating GFP) and a maximum of 42 (β-estradiol activating GFP).
evidence: The results section reports experimental characterization data.

claim: Variations across treatments with pairwise combinations of inducers are contained within 11% of the nominal value for signal concentrations within the range used for circuit experiments.
source: Variations across the treatments are contained within 11% of the nominal value for signal concentrations within the range used for circuit experiments.
evidence: The results section reports experimental data on signal orthogonality.

claim: Positive feedback increased the nonlinearity of the α-factor response from 0.8 ± 0.0 to 1.5 ± 0.1.
source: In both cases, the positive feedback increased the nonlinearity of the response (from 0.8 ± 0.0 to 1.5 ± 0.1 and from 1.0 ± 0.4 to 1.2 ± 0.3 for the α-factor and the auxin case respectively).
evidence: The results section reports experimental data on Hill coefficients.

claim: Positive feedback increased the nonlinearity of the auxin response from 1.0 ± 0.4 to 1.2 ± 0.3.

claim: A mutual-repression topology was used to generate bistability.
source: We opted to use a mutual-repression topology to generate bistability (Gardner et al., 2000; Oyarzún and Chaves, 2015).
evidence: The results section describes the design choice with citations.

claim: The initial two-strain mutual repression circuit generated only a single equilibrium, independently of strain stoichiometry.
source: However, both model simulation and experimental data showed that this circuit can generate only a single equilibrium, independently of the strain stoichiometry (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The results section reports both modeling and experimental results shown in a figure supplement.

claim: Only 0.52% of all possible topologies across network sizes generated non-monotonic behaviors in time.
source: It is worth noticing that only 0.52% of all possible topologies across network sizes generated non-monotonic behaviors in time (of about 106 in total, Figure 5A) and only 0.32% at steady state (of about 105 in total, Figure 5B).
evidence: The results section reports computational analysis results shown in Figure 5.

claim: Only 0.32% of all possible topologies generated non-monotonic behaviors at steady state.
source: It is worth noticing that only 0.52% of all possible topologies across network sizes generated non-monotonic behaviors in time (of about 106 in total, Figure 5A) and only 0.32% at steady state (of about 105 in total, Figure 5B).
evidence: The results section reports computational analysis results shown in Figure 5.

claim: The highest performing time pulse topology is an incoherent feed-forward loop, type 1.
source: The highest performing time pulse topology (Figure 5C) is induced by α-factor that activates both fluorescence expression and auxin synthesis. In turn, auxin induces BAR1 production, which degrades the exogenous α-factor signal: unsurprisingly, this is an incoherent feed-forward loop, type 1 (as in Mangan and Alon, 2003).
evidence: The results section identifies the circuit topology with citation.

claim: Yeast natively synthesizes auxin at saturation.
source: As a matter of fact, these two experiments (Figure 5E F) ended at a higher cell concentration than usual (running time of 12 and 14 hr, respectively), and it is known that yeast natively synthesizes auxin at saturation (Rao et al., 2010).
evidence: The results section cites literature to explain experimental observations.

claim: Synthetic multicellular circuits are modular, easy-to-tune and extendable.
source: We demonstrated through an extensive use of mathematical models, that these synthetic multicellular circuits are modular, easy-to-tune and extendable.
evidence: The discussion summarizes the main findings of the study.

claim: Modularity is achieved through cell-cell communication that avoids cross-talk.
source: Modularity is achieved through cell-cell communication that avoids cross-talk, and is demonstrated by combining input and output of our simple models.
evidence: The discussion explains the mechanism underlying modularity.

claim: The current major limitation in the system is the number of signaling molecules.
source: We imagine this property will gain more practical applications when the number of signaling molecules increases, which is the current major limitation in our system.
evidence: The discussion identifies a limitation of the current system.
